0.0.n: A short reaction showing surprise or hesitation.

0.2.n: Casual form of では, introducing a follow-up question.

0.3.n: A very familiar pronoun that can sound confrontational here.

0.4.n: Marks the person being asked about; the rest of this question is left unstated.

0.6.n: Repeating this pronoun makes the challenge more pointed.

0.7.n: Sets the other person as the topic of the question.

0.8.n: A time word used here without a particle.

0.9.n: Asks which commitment the other person has.

0.10.n: Marks 何 as the thing that exists or is scheduled.

0.11.n: ある describes an existing commitment; the final っ belongs to the following rough quotation expression.

0.12.n: Part of っつんだ, a rough contraction of って言うんだ, not a form of つむ.

0.13.n: Adds force to the speaker's confrontational question.

1.0.n: A noun used alone as a brief answer.

2.3.n: An exaggerated, stretched-out version of 弱い, dismissing the excuse as unimpressive.

2.5.n: Another repetition that reinforces the mocking reaction.

3.0.n: Literally small coins; here it belittles the amount of money earned.

3.1.n: Rough spoken form of 稼ぎたい, expressing a desire to make money.

3.2.n: Limits the person's motive to earning money.

3.3.n: Contraction of では, paired with ねえ in a rough negative expression.

3.4.n: Rough spoken form of ない; together with じゃ and か, it makes an accusatory question.

3.5.n: Ends a rhetorical question that really asserts the accusation.

3.7.n: A hostile, insulting way to address someone.

3.9.n: A forceful call for attention, adding aggression here.

4.1.n: Marks 明日 as the topic.

4.2.n: Placed before 混む to express the highest degree of crowding.

4.3.n: Directly describes 曜日: a day when the place gets busy.

4.4.n: Refers to a recurring weekday rather than a specific date.

4.5.n: The linking form of だ used before explanatory の after a noun.

4.6.n: Gives the statement an explanatory tone.

5.0.n: Rough form of 知らない; here it dismisses the explanation rather than simply reporting ignorance.

5.1.n: Makes the dismissive response more forceful.

5.2.n: Adds a rough, conversational finishing tone to the dismissal.

5.4.n: Shortened form of 何 used before だ.

5.5.n: Plain form of です, completing the blunt question なんだ.

5.6.n: Describes 曜日 within the phrase the speaker is questioning.

5.7.n: Part of the repeated phrase from the other person's explanation.

5.8.n: Casually quotes 混む曜日 as the expression being challenged.

5.10.n: Used as a brief conversational lead-in before the next question.

5.12.n: Short for アルバイト; introduced as the topic without an explicit particle.

5.13.n: Asks what kind of work the person does.

5.14.n: て-form of やる, used in the shortened spoken expression やってんの.

5.15.n: Here ん comes from shortening いる in やっているの to やってんの.

5.16.n: Makes the question casual and asks for an explanation.

6.0.n: First part of 漫喫, an abbreviation of 漫画喫茶; it is not a separate word here.

6.1.n: Second part of 漫喫, short for 喫茶; the complete word names a manga-reading cafe.

7.0.n: First part of 漫喫, repeated here with surprise rather than used independently.

7.1.n: Completes the abbreviation 漫喫; the surprised tone questions the previous answer.

8.0.n: Dismisses the concern rather than praising anything.

8.2.n: Repeating いい makes the reassurance sound impatient and dismissive.

8.4.n: Counts people; this combination is read ひとり.

8.5.n: Downplays the importance of one person's absence.

8.6.n: The connecting form of 行かない, followed by たって to mean even if someone does not go.

8.7.n: This chunk joins たって, meaning even if, with 回る, meaning operations continue; it is not from たつ.

8.9.n: Repeated for emphasis; 回る refers figuratively to a workplace functioning.

8.11.n: Stands in for the workplace already mentioned, avoiding repetition of its name.

9.0.n: A casual way to ask for a reason.

9.1.n: Points back to the other person's dismissive remark.

9.2.n: Refers to what was said, not a physical object.

9.3.n: Plain form; the object marker を after こと is omitted in casual speech.

9.4.n: Asks for an explanation, conveying hurt or disbelief here.

10.0.n: Combines with で to describe an unauthorized absence.

10.1.n: Turns 無断 into a description of how the absence happens.

10.2.n: 欠席する becomes 欠席したら to express a condition.

10.3.n: An English loanword for a punishment or negative consequence.

10.4.n: Marks ペナルティー as what will be applied.

10.5.n: Literally means attach; here it describes receiving a penalty.

11.0.n: Adds another reason supporting the speaker's position.

11.1.n: Specifies when the special staffing arrangement occurs.

11.2.n: Marks 明日 as the topic.

11.3.n: Refers to seasoned workers, not military veterans.

11.4.n: Marks the experienced staff as the people gathering.

11.5.n: Uses 人 to count the experienced workers.

11.6.n: Emphasizes that three experienced workers is an impressively large number.

11.7.n: Describes シフト through the phrase about three experienced workers coming together.

11.8.n: Literally god; slang placed before a noun to praise it as exceptionally good.

11.9.n: Refers to the scheduled work period and its staffing.

11.10.n: Links the noun シフト to explanatory の.

11.11.n: Adds an emphatic explanation of why the speaker values this shift.

0.lit: Huh, then as for you? As for you, what do you say you have tomorrow?
0.tip: っつんだ is a rough shortening of って言うんだ, used here to challenge what someone claims.

1.tip: Japanese often answers questions with just a noun when the context supplies the rest.

2.tip: よわー stretches and shortens 弱い for an exaggerated, mocking reaction.

3.lit: You only want to earn pocket change, isn't that so, you, hey!
3.tip: たい becomes てえ and ない becomes ねえ in this rough style of speech.

4.lit: As for tomorrow, it is the day of the week that gets most crowded, you see.
4.tip: 混む directly modifies 曜日, meaning a day when the place gets crowded.

5.lit: Don't know, huh. What is a crowded weekday? What, your part-time job, what are you doing?
5.tip: やってんの is a casual shortening of やっているの, asking what work the person does.

6.tip: 漫喫 is one abbreviated word from 漫画喫茶, even though it is split into two tap targets.

7.tip: Repeating another person's answer with rising intonation can express disbelief.

8.lit: Fine, fine. Even if just one person doesn't go, it runs, it runs, that kind of place.
8.tip: なくたって means even if not, so 行かなくたって means even if someone doesn't go.

9.lit: Why say that kind of thing?
9.tip: Ending with の asks for an explanation and can express an emotional reaction.

10.lit: If absent without notice, a penalty gets attached…
10.tip: The たら form sets up a condition: if the absence happens, a penalty follows.

11.lit: Besides, tomorrow is an amazing shift where as many as three experienced workers gather!
11.tip: After a number, も emphasizes that the quantity is surprisingly or impressively large.
